newsitem.title: INDIA: Thai baht devaluation rumours "nonsense" -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht devaluation rumours "nonsense" -- minister.

text.p: Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said here on Friday that rumours that the Thai baht would be devalued were "nonsense".

Narongchai told an international conference on Asian economies in the Indian capital that the rise of the U.S. dollar over the past 14 months had prompted rumours that Thailand, which links its currency to the U.S. currency, would devalue the baht.
"Speculation in the media that the baht will be devalued is nonsense," he said. "We don't believe in that."
The Thai baht firmed on Friday and was trading around 25.948/25.950 to the dollar compared with 25.960/25.970 late on Thursday.

A crisis of confidence in the Thai economy appeared to be easing on Friday with a recent run on deposits at 10 troubled finance firms slowing down and the market calming investors digest new government measures, a central bank official said in Bangkok on Friday.
The stock market rose slightly on Friday after plunging this week near to a 4-1/2-year low. It was up 0.76 percent or 5.15 points at 681.80 at 0535 GMT.
The Thai baht firmed early, trading around 25.948/25.950 to the dollar compared to 25.960/25.970 late on Thursday.
On Monday, Thai authorities shook up the finance sector by ordering 10 finance firms, hard-hit by a liquidity crunch, to raise capital by a total of 8.25 billion baht ($317 million).
A Thai newspaper reported on Friday that the government was set to issue zero coupon bonds in an effort to revitalise the sagging stock market.

The Bangkok Post gave few details, saying only that finance ministry officials said the zero coupon bonds would be sold to foreign investors. Ministry officials were not immediately available to comment on the report. ($1= 26 baht)
